facts.text: The Australian Wood Duck looks like a small goose and mostly feeds by grazing in flocks.
facts.quote: This 45–51 cm (18–20 in) duck looks like a small goose, and mostly feeds by grazing in flocks.

facts.text: The male Australian Wood Duck is grey with a dark brown head and a mottled breast.
facts.quote: The male is grey with a dark brown head, mottled breast, and very thin, white-and-black stripes on sides/flanks.

facts.text: The female Australian Wood Duck has white stripes above and below the eye and mottled underparts.
facts.quote: The female has white stripes above and below the eye and mottled underparts.

facts.text: The female's most common call is a loud, rising croaky gnow sound, while the male's is smoother, shorter and higher in pitch.
facts.quote: Their most common call is a loud, rising croaky gnow sound by the females, and male calls are the same except smoother, shorter, and higher in pitch than the females.

facts.text: The Australian Wood Duck lays 9–11 cream-white eggs, and the female incubates them while the male stands guard.
facts.quote: This duck lays 9–11 cream-white eggs, similar to the Mandarin ducks. The female incubates them while the male stands guard.

facts.text: Australian Wood Ducks nest in tree cavities or nest boxes near water, and ducklings leap to the ground to follow their parents.
facts.quote: Australian wood ducks nest in cavities in trees or in nest boxes above or near water. They are lined with a pile of down.

facts.text: The Australian Wood Duck eats grasses, grains, clover and other herbs, and occasionally insects.
facts.quote: The Australian wood duck eats grasses, grains, clover and other herbs, and occasionally, insects.

facts.text: The Australian Wood Duck is rarely seen on open water, preferring to forage in shallow water, grasslands and crops.
facts.quote: It is rarely seen on open water, preferring to forage by dabbling in shallow water, or in grasslands and crops.

facts.text: The Australian Wood Duck has benefited from agriculture and urban development thanks to abundant fresh water sources.
facts.quote: This species has benefited from agriculture and urban development due to the abundance of fresh water sources.

facts.text: The Australian Wood Duck is the only duck with white secondary feathers and dark wingtips when flying.
facts.quote: When flying, the Australian wood duck is the only duck with white secondary feathers and dark wingtips.
